neighbours.label: a quantifier (each, every, several, many, both, hundreds) inside a clause, opening a frequency or amount phrase after a verb or noun
fire: The nurse checked on the patient every hour through the night.
We drove for hours, stopping each time the baby cried.
The farmer sold eggs to his neighbors every Sunday morning.
The tourists were stranded hundreds of miles from the nearest town.
Prices at the store have risen several times this year.
She has won the regional title both times she entered.
The coach reminded the players each week about the rules.
The comet passes close to the earth many times in a millennium.
quiet: The nurse checked on the patient during the long night.
We drove for hours, stopping whenever the baby cried.
The farmer sold eggs to his neighbors on Sunday morning.
The tourists were stranded far away from the nearest town.
Prices at the store have risen sharply this year.
She has won the regional title since she first entered.
The coach reminded the players about the rules again.
The comet passes close to the earth on a long elliptical orbit.

notes: Sentence-initial 'All' scored low in probing; the label is about quantifiers placed mid-clause.
